text_fidelity_a:
Vivid Sports Rainbow Graphite Pickleball Paddle Set, Polymer Honeycomb Core, 1 Neoprene Paddle Cover, Paddle for Men, Women, Children, Supporting The Human Rights Organization, USA Pickleball Approved This is an OK paddle. I don't love it, I don't hate it. I think my favorite thing about this paddle is the colorful design on the paddle face.

The face itself has almost no texture/grit, which as a brand new player may not matter, but will quickly become important after you get the hang of hitting the ball. The paddle face is approximately ~0.5 inches (~13 mm), which is on the thinner side. The upside of a thin paddle is that it provides more power than a thicker paddle, but on the downside, it will be tougher to spin with it (which is compounded by the fact the paddle face has no texture).

Another thing I didn't like was the handle--it feels flat, like a piece of wood. Round handles are much more comfortable in my experience. The grip, however, was pretty nice. It is soft and comfortable to hold, and absorbs sweat pretty well. An added bonus with this paddle is that it comes with a paddle cover. Not a huge deal, but a nice touch nonetheless.

My bottom line is that this is a decent first paddle. Otherwise, I would pass.
text_fidelity_b: Vivid Sports Rainbow Graphite Pickleball Paddle Set, Polymer Honeycomb Core, 1 Neoprene Paddle Cover, Paddle for Men, Women, Children, Supporting The Human Rights Organization, USA Pickleball Approved

text_fidelity_a:
Slime 10056W Bike Tube Puncture Repair Sealant, Prevent and Repair, Suitable for All Bicycles, Non-Toxic, Eco-Friendly, 16oz Bottle Used it, Loved it ... on the single wheel on my electric unicycle (EUC).
Where the rubber meets the road, it seems, doesn't get enough love here. So I thought I'd start a thread to share opinions about tire pressure, maintenance, etc. (starting with some of my opinions).

I find tire pressure to be one of the most important components of handling and ride, and I'm a bit obsessive about it on my EUC's (probably carrying over from motorcycles and bikes). There are three things that make tire pressure a challenge with EUC's:

EUC's only have one tire, low pressure has a direct impact on ride, and tire failures are unforgiving
EUC's have unique bent valve stems that make it hard to find inner-tubes, and a pain to fill (you just don't want to do it)
EUC tire pressure is a bother to check compared to any other vehicle, because the valve stems are hidden in the EUC cavity, and difficult to attach to a pump
... and there are probably other things. The net result is that you want to maintain the tire, fill to pressure and forget it.

To that end, I've Slimed (https://www.amazon.com/Slime-10056-Tube-Sealant-oz/dp/B003V9XYNW/ref=sr_1_2?ie=UTF8&qid=1487706156&sr=8-2&keywords=slime+bicycle) both my V8 and Zero. I used about 1/3rd of the bottle on each one. There is no effect whatsoever on the feel of the wheel, and I think it provides a certain security. In Chicago, I can take my bike into any number of convenient shops to buy and install a new inner-tube; but the same shops would just draw a blank with an EUC, and the inner-tubes are hard to find. Best to maintain what you have.

I like to keep my tire pressure up at 3 bar (~44 psi). The sidewalls of my V8 and Zero tires both recommend 40-65psi pressure, and the V8 comes from the factory at 2.8 bar (~40psi). So for me 3 bar seems the right pressure, and both wheels feel good at that pressure. It's a real bother to fit a pressure gauge on the valve stem because they are bent against the wheel. I almost never get a seal on my gauge without several tries.

So instead, I pumped the wheels up with my Lezyne pump (https://www.amazon.com/Lezyne-Steel-Floor-Drive-Black/dp/B005UND3CY/ref=sr_1_3?ie=UTF8&qid=1487706504&sr=8-3&keywords=lezyne+pump) -- I recommend Lesyzne as the absolute best bike pump on the market -- and then put a Gozens 44psi cap (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01HRIKIY0/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o04_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1) on the wheel. That way, I can easily check the pressure at the start of each ride. You do need to buy the Gozens at a particular pressure (BTW, they have bluetooth systems, which I think are a bit of overkill) but you get 4 of the basic caps for $9, so NBD.
text_fidelity_b: Slime 10056W Bike Tube Puncture Repair Sealant, Prevent and Repair, Suitable for All Bicycles, Non-Toxic, Eco-Friendly, 16oz Bottle

Backyard Champs Corn Hole Outdoor Game: 2 Folding Cornhole Boards and 8 Bean Bags, Aluminum Frame with MDF Board Cornhole is a fun game that brings back memories of “Toss-Across” for me. I never had heard of, or played, cornhole until it was introduced to me at a social gathering relatively recently. I have wanted my own set for taking to family functions and picnics with friends, and this set is well suited for these situations.

I will start with this: I received the tailgate version which is a little smaller than the regulation size set. The difference is that the boards are a foot shorter. That’s ok, but it does mean that my set is not suitable for true tournament play and instead is geared for casual competition. Both sized sets are available here; make sure you get the size you want. While it may be a little smaller, it has two distinct advantages. First, it is lighter so it is easier to carry. Second, because it is smaller it is more compact and can be stored (and transported) more easily too.

This set is made to be portable. Most sets I have seen have been made of plywood and have fixed legs. To move them is awkward and often unwieldy. This set instead has an aluminum frame and lightweight boards so the weight is substantially reduced. The legs fold under, allowing the set to lay flat. This makes it a lot easier to pack the set for travel and to store it away when not in use. An important detail – when the legs are down they lock in place with a metal bracket so the board will not collapse.

The set comes with 8 bean bags, 4 blue and 4 red. These are regulation size and are interchangeable with other sets.

So far my family is very pleased with this set. It is made very well, it is compact and portable, and because this set (in my case) is the tailgate version it is lighter and easier to store when not in use. This is an easy product to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Backyard Champs Corn Hole Outdoor Game: 2 Folding Cornhole Boards and 8 Bean Bags, Aluminum Frame with MDF Board

Sunny Health & Fitness Magnetic Recumbent Exercise Bike with Silent Belt Drive, Performance Monitor, BMI and Body Fat Calculator, 275 LB Max Weight - SF-RB4953 So far, so good! Assembling this exercise bike went pretty smoothly. I didn't have any issues getting through the instructions and had no missing pieces/parts, which is always a plus! As soon as it was assembled, I was excited to give it a try. I am 5'2 and my husband is 6'. The seat adjusts pretty easily and without much effort. We didn't have any trouble transitioning at all. It does take a little trial and error finding your "sweet spot", but I think that that would be the case with any bike. The seat and backing are comfortable and support you well. After a few minutes of using the bike, it felt great (unlike traditional bikes in my opinion). I really like the information that is displayed on the screen: time, speed, distance, calories, and pulse (the monitors are on the two side bars). You can choose to have it focus on one aspect or cycle between them. Personally, I like for it to move through them. The monitor turns on and off by itself which is nice as well. You can choose between 8 levels that adjust the tension. At first, I did not notice much of a difference, but after a few minutes you can definitely feel it!

Ultimately, I think that this was a great purchase. It's easy to use and a more comfortable way to transition into exercising more often. Now I have only had it for a day, so these are just my initial thoughts and opinions. I would like to use it for a week or two and then I can update my review!

I had the opportunity to purchase this item at a discount in exchange for an honest, unbiased review.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Magnetic Recumbent Exercise Bike with Silent Belt Drive, Performance Monitor, BMI and Body Fat Calculator, 275 LB Max Weight - SF-RB4953

As a former certified personal trainer, I own and have used probably more functional training equipment, e.g., bands, balls, etc. than most gyms have.

I consulted with a physiatrist and after he told me that if I could find a way to use exercise bands without bending my wrists, I could do pushing and pulling exercises for back, chest and shoulders (and arms). I bought these cuffs, attached carabiner hooks to the d-rings, attached the cuffs to my wrists and the other end of the carabiner to the nylon web handle of an exercise band with nylon webbing around a pole or in a door jamb to anchor it.

Pelican Full Set of Genuine Storm Replacement Multi-Layer Cubed Foam for iM2100 Storm Case I use this foam in a Pelican case which holds sensitive electronic equipment, the sort which is rectangular in size. I've tried many other kinds of foam - stiffer foam which doesn't yield easily, softer foam which does, but nothing beats the cubes for usability. I used razors, art knives, rulers and extreme care, but it in the end the shapes always came out ragged, rough, and far from square. I doubt I could manage a really clean job without an actual laser cutter.

This bypassed the need for all of that. Basically, the foam pad comes pre-cut, except for a very thin layer of foam in the very middle of the pad. It is a simple matter to pluck out the cubes - really, the little square columns of foam - in the approximate shape of what you want to store in the case. I haven't had any issues with too many cubes coming out at once, if you use even the slightest care, you can be sure that you are removing only exactly what you need to. Each column is about 1/4" square I believe.

The set comes with an undulating top insert, and a solid bottom insert, as well as two pluckable cube inserts for the middle.

I would definitely recommend this as the replacement foam for the Pelican case over alternatives. It might not be as good as inserts which have been custom-shaped to components, but it is about as close as you can get.

Birchwood Casey Shoot-N-C, 8" Targets, Adhesive, See Hits Instantly At the time I bought this 30 pack the price was $20 delivered for a per-target price of $0.66 each. This is a great value, as the local Wal-Mart sells a pack that is about $1 each.

Each target is a peel-and-stick "label". It adheres excellent to cardboard and clean, flat surfaces. I adheres OK to rougher surfaces like old, splintering plywood. I affixed this directly to an old shot-up apple crate and ended up having to supplement a little duct tape to keep it on when the wind kicked up.

Every target has four "pasties" that you can peel off and affix to the target after you've shot it. Each pasty is large enough to cover 2 or 3 .45 caliber holes, depending on how close your grouping is. The pasties are useful enough to extend each target by at least one more shooting group.

Here is a great suggestion to really extend the life of each target -- if you have guns of multiple calibers, start with your lowest caliber and work your way up. You can easily tell the difference between your .22 caliber hitsvs. your 9mm vs. your .45 caliber.

Using this methodology, you could probably use a single target up to 6 times, unless you are a nail driver and shoot out your bullseye really quickly!

The only downsides I can say are:

1) These targets are much more expensive than paper targets, but they're so easy to see that they're totally worth it for practicing your shooting and making adjustments after each shot.

2) The pasties can sometimes fly off when they get hit. Make sure you give them a good press and seal.
text_fidelity_b: Birchwood Casey Shoot-N-C, 8" Targets, Adhesive, See Hits Instantly

text_fidelity_a: Ultimate Body Press Ceiling Mount Pull Up Bar for 8 Foot Ceilings, Steel Through-Bolted 48” Straight Bar with 14” Risers, Fits 16”and 24” Joist Spacing, Max 450lbs, USA Designed and Backed I installed a pull up bar using pipes from a hardware store previously.  The issue was weakness at the pipe threads.  Because I was concerned about getting injured, I shopped around and this was the only I could find for around 100$ that had a non-moving bar.  I also wanted a simple single bar, not a double bar. The pros are it is easy to install, it doesn’t budge, even when I (accidentally) kip. I weight 220 pounds, so that says a lot.  The bar is appropriate length and circumference for a proper grip.  I am 5’7 and installed on 9 foot rafters it’s perfect. I need to hop up or use small step.  This is good, as I don’t want my feet to touch the ground. The screws, nuts and bolts are correct. The disadvantage is it’s expensive for what it is, three pieces of painted metal and some nuts and bolts with a greasy wrench and hex..  The “wrench” is kind a joke,  it It can be used.  A drill bit would have been more useful. The grip is too smooth, like most pull up bars. Like most fitness equipment, grips are either too smooth, or knurled to the point they rip up your hands. I use tennis ratchet grips (it took six) to wrap it.  It is probably a foot too wide, not an issue, as you could attach accessories to the extra space and do really wide pull ups. It would be helpful for it to include a cutout on the box for install.  You definitely need another person or straps to install it. Time will tell, but it’s great so far.  I do think it’s a bit expensive for what it is, but nothing else really compares.  The inconveniences are minor, so would recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Ultimate Body Press Ceiling Mount Pull Up Bar for 8 Foot Ceilings, Steel Through-Bolted 48” Straight Bar with 14” Risers, Fits 16”and 24” Joist Spacing, Max 450lbs, USA Designed and Backed

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version) FitBit Charge 2 HeartRate and Fitness Wristband.
Update: I have been using this watch for 6 months.
Pros-
App-I have used the mobile app and the program on the computer to use the product. The app is very nice, user friendly.
HeartRate Function-I like the heart rate function. Just knowing my heart rate at various times of the day and night, and while working out is important to me.
Multi-Sport Tracking-I like choosing which exercise I am going to do on the watch.
Cons- The watch does not keep track of how many miles I bike ride when using the exercise bike. The watch only records the amount of time I am on the bike. Then it transfers a number to amount of floors I have climbed instead of miles on the bike.
Smart Watch Notification- I have to be near my mobile device for the notification to work.
Band is Too Wide-I do not like the size of the band. The band is too wide for my preference.
Size of Watch. I had to return the first watch I purchased. I had choosen the large size and it was too big. My wrist is 6 inches, thats 15cm. The size small is still too big for my wrist. Their are 10 notches in the watch to adjust it to for length. I wear mine 6 notches from the top!
Watch Not Comfortable to sleep with. The band is too large to be comfortable to sleep with.

Pure Pulse Heart Rate-The FitBit Charge 2 has a continous heart rate. It is really nice to be able to monitor heart rate while working out, especially when using the treadmill.
All day Activity-The watch tracks your activity all day (including amount of steps, floors climbed, interval training, treadmill, weights, workout, elliptical, running, bike, heart monitor, and calories burned). The activity can be transferred to the app.
Sleep-The watch tracks your sleep. After you sleep you can transfer the information to the app to view how well you slept. It shows how many times you woke up, how many times you were restless.
Multi-Sport Tracking-You choose on your watch what workout you will do. The watch tracks your progress and heart rate. After exercising transfer the information to the app. You can see all of the information including graphs of heart rate, intensity of workout. The choices are treadmill, weights, workout, elliptical, running, and bike.
Smartphone Notifications, and Interchangeable Bands. Their are different choices for the watch band and they are available for purchase separately.
Size-Compair between Small and Large. The difference between the Small and the Large is the length of the wristband. The length of the small band is 5.5-6.9 inch (13.9cm- 17.5 cm). The length of the large is 6.3-8.2 inch (16.0-20.8).
The app- You can Run the app using a mobile device or a computer. With the computer you use a web site instead of an app. The site is FitBit.com The FitBit Dashboard is available on the app or on the computer. View on the dashboard: steps, calories burned, floors, active minutes, sleep, weight goals, calories burned, cups to drink, vibrate alarm, clock faces, and graphs. The graphs are: calorie intake and burn, steps, distance, floors, time active, sleep, and weight. Connect with friends to inspire and compete in challenges, weight goals and food logging, and celebrate milestones with badges. 2PCS Yellow LED Flash Tyre Wheel Valve Cap Light for Car Bike bicycle Motorbicycle Wheel Light Tire Light for Night Safety by TheBigThumb I initially bought this product because of the pictures and how it resembled a constant glow like in the movie TRON. I already was warned in the reviews that the product so not continuously stay on which was fine, with the cheap price it was a risk worth taking. Now that being said, when I received the product, I it not immediately obvious which light is what color. I had to set it up which was simple and test it out. These lights are motion activated with very low sensitivity, so the bumbs will need to be frequent or near constant in order for them to light up. Becuase these lights are on a wheel and the force exerted on the lights moves in a circular motion, the lights will not light up just because the wheel is spinning but rather when the tire hit a strong enough resistance in the road or rocks or gaps in the sidewalk. These lights probably wouldn't light up on a wheel that is operating on a smooth enough track or road. I tested it on my bike and the "blinking" lights were cool from a first person point of view, I have yet to test the "coolness" factor of the lights from a third person perspective (or in other words I am not geting any positive feedback from passer's by. I did not test this product on my car or on a motor cycle (like in the packaging).

With all that said, the price was low enough, the product was plastic, was shinny enough, and the performance is adequate. Overall the product is worth the risk! for cyclist or bike enthusiasts. I would definitely recommend this for the children in your family who won't care much about the quality of this inexpensive product.
text_fidelity_b: 2PCS Yellow LED Flash Tyre Wheel Valve Cap Light for Car Bike bicycle Motorbicycle Wheel Light Tire Light for Night Safety by TheBigThumb

text_fidelity_a:
Kelty TN 2 Person Tent The Kelty TN2 tent was very easy to set up, take down and repack into the cube styled sack. Aluminum poles are light, clips are smart, stargazing option is awesome and there are 2 small interior pockets perfect for holding eyeglasses. I tried really hard to find something to criticize about this backpacking 4 1/2 pound tent but did not succeed. Even the colors are attractive, with a gray base and contemporary light grassy green complementary pairing. The fly adds room for storing the gear we don't want inside the tent and the ability to enter/exit from either side is freeing especially for those with a tendency for claustrophobia. One is larger than the other and I am very curious about why -- assume it was an intentional design to increase the durability and structure.

We first set up the tent in the house and even the dog loved being comfy inside our little den. Two adults and a small dog were comfortable and not bumping into each other or the walls. When we used it outside and we could see a real sky above with the stargazer setup, we experienced a freedom and airiness that was quite close to sleeping tent-free. It literally took a minute to unwrap, drop and attach the fly when we wanted to be covered and protected. Condensation was reduced by the fly mesh openings with their arched cover and the pair of little clear triangle sections could be covered for privacy when camping an a more public area. This tent is suitable for moderate weather but I personally would not use it in a harsh environment. We are purchasing the [[ASIN:B00HQZB39O Kelty TN 2 Footprint]] which I think will also fit into the Kelty sack.

The aluminum poles are quick to snap into position and the curve of the head sections makes for a very tall tent for this footprint. We are not tall, so the interior seemed palatial even when we were moving around. The clamping system is very smart, you turn it perpendicular to the pole, put the pole in the center of the clip, then snap it into place for a very secure grab and fit. Removing it is just as quick and the pole sections pop and fold smoothly. The pair of poles is joined at the intersection, so it is less cumbersome than using two separate poles. The third pole fits easily across the top and with a tent system using color coding, intuition kicks in for those who don't want to read the instruction manual.

text_fidelity_a:
Withings Go | Activity & Sleep tracker I spent hours trying to get this Nokia Health Mate Go ("Nokia") to work.

Bottom line: This is a worthless piece of junk.

Here is what I did:

1. I installed the Nokia on my iPhone 5c with associated app. The app indicated that it recognized the Nokia.
2. I put it on my left wrist and walked all over my house to test its pedometer's accuracy in counting steps. After ten minutes, it still registered zero steps. Clearly it did not record or update steps properly.
3. I tried to figure out why the device, in this regard, was not communicating well with the iPhone app. I finally employed the computer programmer's tried-and-true cure-all: I did the nearest to a "reboot" that I could. I killed the app and then restarted it.
4. I started walking again, and it was at least trying to record the steps. But all it did was state, "Looking for your tracker...."
5. Finally the app updated, and then it started to finally count steps. I then killed the app and started it again to refresh it.
6. I did a test. I walked while counting my steps myself, speaking them out loud. After 165 steps, I looked down at the Nokia. It said I had taken 55 steps.

This thing is a bust as a pedometer, and I couldn't figure out anything else it is useful for. Of all things, it can't even measure the heart rate.

This is NOT a cheaper alternative to a Fitbit. It is not good for anything. If you want a pedometer, I suggest buying one.
text_fidelity_b: Withings Go | Activity & Sleep tracker

Even though I had a trust in the brand name, I was also prepared to be disappointed because of the past bad experience with others (Zippo etc.). This one worked on the first try after only about 5 seconds of lighting, I couldn't believe it!! The burner(Catalyst) even glows red in the dark. It takes a little time before the burner warms up the whole body and pushes more vapor through the burner, then it gets really warm, or rather hot.
Besides its usefulness for normal cold day activity, this makes a great survival tool under extreme cold condition. Remember the family stranded in the snow for over a week and husband died by trying to get rescue several years back? In the situation like that, this Peacock and a bottle of lighter fluid will decide your fate.
Don't even try other brands(I have two) and waste your money. You pay more for a Peacock but you'll be sure to get the working hand warmer.
Later, I'm planning to try this in home made Kotatsu and see how well it'll perform but I know I maybe too optimistic. Even if it's half way warm as regular kotatsu heater, the cost of running it will be far cheaper, it's worth a try.

Stanley The Quadvac Trigger Action Mug, Canvas, 16OZ This is the best thermos I've owned to date, but it's far from perfect.

If you put piping hot coffee in it, it will keep it hot for about 45 minutes, and keep it warm for about 2 more hours after that. I haven't used it for cold drinks.

I love the handle style; that's my favorite part about it. Most handled thermoses have this infuriating issue of the mouthpiece never lining up properly with where the handle is, so you always have to hold them weirdly to drink from them. On this thermos, the handle is fabric, and can be adjusted 360 degrees around the thermos, so no matter where the mouthpiece ends up, you can just adjust the handle to be right where you need it. the other nice thing about the fabric handle is that you won't break it by bumping it into things or dropping it.

The worst part about this thing is cleaning it. The entire head of it is very complex, with lots of moving parts, springs, and plastic bits - ALL of which are submerged in whatever you are drinking. So, when you take the lid off, you have disassemble the whole thing and either soak all the parts, or wash them all individually. Don't be lazy and put off cleaning it until the next day or you'll have whatever you drank caked all though the innards. If you don't mind keeping it clean, it's really nice. I'm very happy with it.
text_fidelity_b: Stanley The Quadvac Trigger Action Mug, Canvas, 16OZ

Compact Camp Stool Folding Ultralight Portable Mini Chair for Camping Fishing Hiking Gardening Beach Outdoor Chair for Kid Alduts I received this portable camping chair from the manufacturer at no cost for evaluation, and here are my thoughts.

This portable chair is great for camping, backpacking, and attending outdoor events. Weighing les than 2 pounds, it comes in a sturdy storage back with a handle and loops so it can be carried by hand, tucked away with gear, or lashed to a pack without taking much space or adding much weight, and it's so easy to set up my ten year old can do it in about 2 minutes.

The support frame is made of lightweight aircraft aluminum sections attached to each other by shock cord, so you just slip the sections together, secure the ends into the plastic housing, and then attach the ends to the slots in the chair. It's easier if you attach the bottom before the back. When assembled the bottom of the seat is approximately 14" from the ground, the seat is about 21" across, and the back is about 26" high.

I found that the chair sits well on the ground and it feels very stable. The material conforms to the shape of the body so it provides good support, but it does sit very low to the ground so people with arthritis, sciatica, hip problems, or mobility issues might find it difficult to get into or out of without assistance. The chair will support an adult weighting up to 260 pounds, but my 10 year old already decided that it's perfect for her so it's now going to be her chair.

The chair is easy to dissemble and put back in the carry bag, when you're finished using it, and it hardly takes any space at all to store. We really like this chair and think it's perfect for camping, fishing, outdoor concerts or any other outdoor event.

text_fidelity_a:
Weaver Leather Throw Line Storage Bag Are you a ham radio operator tossing portable antennas up into trees? Don't like the idea of sling shots and potato launchers? Hate that tangled mess of mason line? Looking for reasonable elevation for the weekend? I recommend this.

I hate rope, string, wine, wire, cable, and anything squiggly that is over 25 feet long. It is certain to become a tangled mess and cost 30 minutes to an hour to straighten out just to have it wrap around your ankle and trip you up. Happens to me every single time.

Some smart ham out there suggested I try this throw line bag and weight. After it was delivered I brought it out to the backyard and started tossing it around. I made about five or six long low tosses without any tangles and three or four high tosses over the tree without a problem. I'm sold on it. My slingshot is going to see a lot less use and I still don't have the guts to try my potato launcher.

The bag is more than storage. After a toss you just stuff the line back in the bag without concern for winding it properly. Just push it down in the bag. When tossing the weight you just let the line play out of the bag. I have yet to experience a tangle. I'm sure there's some added resistance and I might be losing a foot or two of max height but for ease of storage and deployment you can have the foot.

When done, stuff the line in the bag along with the weight. Cinch it up and toss back in the truck until next time. Not a whole lot of fussing.

A warning... wear gloves. The rope they use burns! Me and one other person found out the hard way. Ya... I didn't tell him. But even after that he went out and bought his own kit so maybe the burn wasn't so bad. Still, wear gloves.

I think I got the 12 oz weight. Then next one down might have been a little better. After a few tosses of the 12 oz weight I was getting real tired and my height/distance was dropping rapidly. Good argument for doing it right the first time I guess. Still, 8 oz might be some benefit.

I know it's tempting but don't toss this thing at your buddies. The weight is substantial and if you hit them they won't share in your amusement. Not that I did anything like that but you know. It could happen.

That's it. Wish I found this a long time ago. Until now I had been using my slingshot with a 1 oz weight and a Zebco 33 and 20 lb test line. Then I would tie the mason line for the second pass. The tangles were unbelievable so a spool of mason line was a one-time-use item for me. The rope in this kit is strong enough to hold up any wire antenna for a weekend so you only need a single pass.
text_fidelity_b: Weaver Leather Throw Line Storage Bag

NIYIKOW 2 Pack Grip Strength Trainer, Hand Grip Strengthener, Adjustable Resistance 22-132Lbs (10-60kg), Non-Slip Gripper, Perfect for Musicians Athletes and Hand Injury Recovery I received this as a review sample and have been using it for a little over a week. Prior to receiving this one I had been using a pair of compression rings, so my exercise regimen was already established.

This has pros and cons over the simpler rings. On the pro side I can adjust the resistance of the grip, allowing me to progressively work my way from easier to harder exercises. On the con side a pair of these is a lot more expensive than the rings that I had been using.

After a week of using this on the minimum resistance setting (where I intend to keep it) the transition from the rings I was using to this was seamless. My normal exercises continued with no real changes to the routine, and this grip is not as easy to misplace as the rings.

Since I had been doing hand strength exercises for quite some time before using this device I can speak to the long term benefits of those (using any device). The strength such exercises develop and the working of muscles and joints are a hedge against the aging process because at sixty-six I was starting to feel the effects of age. Since my 'day job' is professional drummer my hands are important and this - and, to be fair, the rings I was using - keep my hands in shape. More importantly, they build strength and stamina.

Bottom line: this grip works, is well made, and can truly make a difference if you consistently use it.

text_fidelity_a:
EcoVessel Summit TriMax Triple Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Flip Straw - 24 Ounces I thought for sure this would be my final bottle. Double stainless steel + a copper lining? Sounds amazing. Tall and thinner than most so it fits in cup holders? Nice! Multiple lid options available for purchase? Cool.

Thing is I tried this next to my other bottles and this was by far the worst at keeping drinks cold. Ice melted in 3 hours or less every time I tried, that’s with half a tray of ice cubs + refrigerated water. All others kept the ice solid for at least 6+ hours.

The style of the bottle is a 5. But if it cannot keep ice from melting and drinks cold as long as my other bottles and tumblers? It’s useless to me. May be good for at home when you can constantly refresh ice and drinks. When traveling? It’s not going to work for me and that’s the main reason I got it. I feel very disappointed especially when they send me emails bragging about how they keep drinks colder way longer than others claim to. They don’t they’re the opposite or what they claim to be.

I tried to review it on their site, but couldn’t get it approved so the product has 5 stars there but I wouldn’t trust that star count.

*update* got a different brand and decided to compare how fast they lose their ability to stay cool. This bottle went from 35 degree water to 66.3 in 3.5 hours. While the other bottle took over 24 hours to get that warm.
text_fidelity_b: EcoVessel Summit TriMax Triple Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Flip Straw - 24 Ounces

text_fidelity_a: FoldyLock Clipster Folding Bike Lock - Award Winning Wearable Compact Bicycle Lock - Ultra Sleek Lightweight Smart Bike Security Accessory with Key Set for Bikes E Bikes and Scooters - 75 cm The Clipster folding lock is very well designed.  As you fold it up the sectional lock links click into place and a silicon band secures the rest.  The result is a silent lock when you are riding, and it also comes with a belt clip so that you don't have to attach anything to the bike.  This is my second folding lock, I also have the Abus, a well-known brand that I have been using for about 5 years.  It is an excellent lock, but the Foldy has improved on that design.  The Foldy is considerably heavier, maybe half as much again, and I thought it would drag my belt and pants down but that didn't happen.  The Foldy is very quiet, something I am particular about.  The Abus comes in a plastic box that you velcro to the frame and it rattles around abominably in there so I threw the case away and began to secure the Abus with a length of velcro to quieten it down.  The Clipster has designed that modification in, while also securing the linkages and adding the belt clip.  In terms of diameter, both locks are the same, so you won't be hitching up to a thick pole, but any skinny street sign or bike rack will be fine.  The price point for both locks is the same.  3 keys provided.

text_fidelity_a:
AIRELAX Sleeping pad for Camping, Ultralight and Compact Inflatable Sleeping Mat, Ultimate for Camping, Backpacking, Hiking,Sleeping Bag, Cot, Apple Green This pad is pretty much exactly what it says, a decent non-insulated pad that packs super small and is decently comfortable. I laid on it next to a Klymit Static V that I also own and the two were pretty much equals in terms of cushion. At a little over 200lbs I didn't bottom out on my hips which I've had problems with in the past with other cheap pads.
The stuff sack works as a decent pump sack, requiring between 12 and 13 cycles to fully fill the pad. The pad says it's 2.2 inches thick, With a pair of calipers I found it to be almost exactly 2 inches. Inflated at it's widest point, it's right about 22 inches, not including the seams. It's 74 inches long when inflated. It packs smaller than any other pad I won at roughly 10x3.5. Including the stuff sack it weighs 15.4 ounces, less than advertised!

My only complaints are have to do with the valve. It doesn't feel very robust, as the rubber component sort of just flops around until it's under pressure from the inside. This means it needs to be babysat a lot more when you're trying to deflate the pad to keep the rubber flap open so air can escape. It does allow for small adjustments to the pad firmness by gently pressing on the rubber part. My other issue with with valve placement. Its at the foot. That makes it really hard to adjust while lying down, which is exactly when you would want to adjust it.
